bullets.text: Machine learning involves teaching computers to learn from data.
It focuses on learning patterns instead of explicit rules.
Supervised learning trains systems on labeled data.
Example: An email marked as spam or not spam.
The model learns patterns to predict unseen cases.
Common algorithms include decision trees, support vector machines, and neural networks.
The system finds patterns in data without labels.
Example: Clustering customers into groups based on purchasing behavior.
K-means is a classic example of an unsupervised algorithm.
An agent interacts with an environment to learn.
Learning occurs from feedback or rewards.
Example: Training an AI to play video games.
Another example is controlling a robot.
Overfitting: Model memorizes training data.
Overfitting leads to poor performance on new, unseen data.
Bias: Occurs when the training data itself is not balanced.
Healthcare: Used for disease prediction.
Finance: Applied in fraud detection.
Self-driving cars: Essential for object recognition.
The next lecture will cover evaluation metrics.
Key metrics include accuracy, precision, and recall.
The F1-score will also be discussed.
